newsitem.title: FRANCE: French bill to implement chemical weapons ban.
newsitem.headline: French bill to implement chemical weapons ban.

text.p: France introduced a bill Wednesday setting out controls needed to implement a world ban on chemical weapons.

The bill, presented to the cabinet by Industry Minister Franck Borotra, will make it compulsory for industrialists to declare chemical weapons as well as manufacturing and storage facilities so that they can be destroyed.
Prior government permission will be required to produce chemicals that could be used to make weapons.
Government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said the bill would affect 333 industrial facilities in France.

The 1993 United Nations convention banning the development, production, stockpiling and use of chemical weapons and calling for the destruction of the weapons and their production facilities will come into force on April 29.
It has been signed by at least 160 countries including all five permanent members of the Security Council -- the United States, Russia, Britain, China and France.
